title: Invitation of Members of Parliament to School Events
what_it_is: Invitation of Members of Parliament to School Events

sections.label: Schools and partisan politics
sections.summary: Schools do not invite or accede to requests by MPs or political parties to speak at school events, keeping schools free of partisan politics.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Schools do not invite or accede to requests by any Member of Parliament (MP) or political party to speak at school events.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Schools are to be kept free of partisan politics, so people should not be speaking in their capacity as a member of a political party attending a school for an event.

sections.label: Keeping partisan politics out of schools
sections.summary: Schools are to be kept free of partisan politics, and the Member should make a case if he wants partisan politics in schools.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Schools are to be kept free of partisan politics.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The framing that the Member made in the supplementary question suggests that, actually, the intention is for him or whoever he is speaking on behalf of, his party, to attend and represent political views.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: This is not the intention of what we do in schools.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: If the Member would like to make a case as to why there should be partisan politics in schools, then I think that is the case that he should make.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We take the view that partisan politics should be kept out of schools.
